vessa-corran-dov.why: A Flats soup-line preacher in cheap entry Heavy plate (Sanctified kit wants heavy) with a plain service pistol she'd rather not draw, a knife, a burner and the medical kit that keeps the lamp-room a clinic four mornings a week; no chrome, because the Veil erodes under metal and she is Corran-stubborn about staying flesh.

kaes-vahn-estal.why: Unarmoured by kit doctrine (Hexshot is an armor:none caster kit), the Static Saint carries a capacitive Seraph Mercy because a Stormcaller's sidearm should throw the same element he does, a holdout in the sleeve out of patron-house habit, and a fake SIN because the Spires filed him as a liability; no chrome at all — magic erosion, and Soft-grade implants don't exist as pack SKUs yet.

barak-voss-hallor.why: The Foreman negotiates in demolition plate on purpose: the Juggernaut kit's heavy weapon is the IW Barrage-12 LMG, the Argent Mint Persuader is the part of the conversation that doesn't need bullets, and the story's hydraulic ram forearm and plated torso are literally the Cyberlimb (5 BI) and Dermal Plating (4 BI) — 9 of 20 spent, credstick and fake SIN because a fixer closes deals with both.

wren-sable-corvin.why: The Kite wears an unremarkable armored coat she can shrug off before she changes, carries the Greenline Longwatch marksman rifle her Longshot kit calls for and a pocket pistol for the climb down, and takes no chrome — implanted metal doesn't fold into a raven, and the long sight is already in her eye.

mods.why: 0.3.45 — a Technomancer has no deck, so his Whiteout magazine is compiled into Wired Native (the class Item that is his host); two fires loaded.

sabbat-vane.why: A dead man in ballistic-weave streetwear that reads as ordinary clothes, one cheap pistol he barely uses, a fake SIN because the coffin-motel wants a living renter, and a Faraday bag to keep the ghosts he's carrying off the grid; a Technomancer's Resonance is the worst thing to put metal next to, so his one implant is grown, not bolted: Soft Cyber-Ears, a cultured cochlear lattice for hearing the dead frequency (1 Body Integrity, Soft grade, so no Resonance cap lost on its own).

vira-kellis-nade.why: The Warren-Wire dresses in soft ballistic weave that squeezes through a duct grille with her, keeps a compact pistol as a last resort, and does her real work through a Fleet Deck RCC; a Datajack (1 BI) is the rigger’s minimum, and Skillwires (4 BI) is the socket that runs her Targeting Soft — 5 of 20 Body Integrity, the least metal a Wererat can carry and still jump in shooting.

kessic-draye.why: Null keeps the Street Deck he already carries and adds the two programs a Disruptor runs on the way in — Sneak to stay quiet and Crash to dissolve cheap ICE — plus a compiled Whiteout magazine (2 fires, 1 of 2 Street Deck slots) to scrub Trace; a holdout in the sleeve for the meat that's left behind; the port behind his ear from the story is the Datajack (1 BI) and the optics that read a lattice of light are Cyber-Eyes (2 BI), 3 of 20.

renn-solace-ward.why: Patchwire works out of the bag, so the kit is the class's own Quick Build (Gunslinger: light armor, medium weapon) and the armor is the cheap jacket he can cut off a patient and put back on himself; the Field Surgery Kit and Slap-Doc Kit are the table, the Trauma Patch is what he hands over when the table is not an option, and the IW Journeyman is a service pistol he would rather keep holstered. A basic fake SIN because an unlicensed doc who files paperwork stops being a doc. No chrome at all: he is Pure Human and the whole point of him is that the block has somewhere to go that is not a ripperdoc.

kade-orrin-vex.why: Hardframe is the ADDENDUM's lock written out: a Cyborg has 25 Body Integrity and Michael wants every point of it visible, so all seven Standard-grade implants go on and nothing is left over — Wired Reflexes 6, Cyberlimb Arm 5, Muscle & Bone Lacing 5, Dermal Plating 4, Cyber-Eyes 2, Cyber-Ears 2, Datajack 1, exactly 25 of 25. No Soft-grade substitutions: subtle is the opposite of the brief. 0.3.125 (C3) re-cuts the *gear* half to Echelon 1, because he is an E1 hero: the Milspec Battledress (E2) and the IW Bastion (E3) were both above his band, and the rifle is two-handed, which a Warframe cannot hold alongside the shield its own doctrine asks for. He now carries the Security Rig — E1 heavy armor, and corp-sec issue reads right on an ex-corp frame — a Riot Shield, a Argent Sovereign .50 for range, and a Shock-Stick as the one-handed imposing/stun mace, which is what "medium weapon plus a shield" actually looks like at street prices. The chrome, the Body Integrity spend and the fiction behind them are untouched.
